events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The case is filed as a safety dispute. The rider's complaint states the driver "threatened to lock me in when I asked to get out," and the in-app chat record corroborates the sequence: at 17:09 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3], and one minute later the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Read in context, that message is a threat of confinement made in response to a rider's request to exit the vehicle — conduct aimed at the rider and intimidation of a passenger, which the code of conduct barring "abuse of any kind" reaches; both messages are timestamped in a complete 2-message record [F5], so nothing about the exchange is in doubt. Under SAFE-1, where threats or intimidation appear in the chat, complaint or driver statement, the judge must not decide the case automatically but must escalate with a factual summary for human handling.

The driver's written statement [F6] offers a self-defence account — that the rider tried to open the door at the lights and he told her to sit down "for her own safety and drove on" — and this, not any route or fare question, is the factual dispute a human reviewer must resolve. The safety screen is asymmetric, so a suspected threat cannot be resolved in-house even though the driver's motive is contested. Escalation is also the only outcome the policy execution trace allows here, since the SAFE-1 screen returned ✓ and no refund or waiver computation is in issue.

The route-fare record itself raises no deviation claim: actual distance was 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (−0.1 km, −0%) [F1], and duration 23.7 min against 21.8 min estimated (+1.9 min) [F2]. The trip was a fixed-quote RydeX fare of $32.86, so under RD-2 the non-metered branch would yield no mileage-based refund; in any event the fare is not the disputed item and I compute no amount. Both advocates requested no_action, but neither brief was argued (judge-only ablation) and neither addresses the SAFE-1 threshold; a no_action disposition is unavailable where the chat contains a threat [F4].

Profiles play no part in the outcome: the rider's clean history [F7] and the driver's 1038 trips with 0 disputes [F8] neither establish nor rebut the safety allegation, and profile facts cannot decide a case alone. Flagging of the account is not ordered by me, because RD-6 (route disputes upheld) and NS-2 (arrival-button abuse) are not engaged on these facts; the appropriate disposition is referral to a human reviewer.
